segments.title: 第163章 會死的
segments.content:
Renewing My Verdant Youth Chapter 163: I'll Die

After dinner, Xu Youyu and Yan Zhusheng obediently cleared the dining table and went to the kitchen to wash the dishes.

This left only Li Luo and Ying Chanxi in the living room.

Li Luo rubbed his full stomach, got up, and went to the piano room. He brought out his guitar, sat on the sofa, and looked at Ying Chanxi. "At noon, you said you wanted to hear a new song. Want to listen now?"

Ying Chanxi glanced at the backs of the two girls in the kitchen and walked over to sit down beside Li Luo. "Should we wait for Senior and Zhusheng to finish the dishes and listen together?"

"It's fine, they can hear it from here too." Li Luo strummed the strings, preparing to get into the mood.

Seeing that he was about to play, Ying Chanxi didn't object any further. She hugged the Pikachu and Doraemon plushies on the sofa tightly, squeezed their heads, and quietly immersed herself in Li Luo's song.

After Li Luo finished singing, Ying Chanxi gradually came back to her senses and asked curiously, "Is this the song your rock club has been practicing recently? Are you planning to sing it at the New Year's Gala?"

"Yes." Li Luo smiled. "We've pretty much perfected it."

"Then I'll look forward to it." Ying Chanxi put her legs together, then asked, "On the day of the New Year's Gala, will your class's mini-game be busy?"

"It's alright." Li Luo thought for a moment. "From eight to eleven-thirty in the morning, I'll have to help out in our classroom for about an hour. It's for that 'Guess the Instrument' game. I have to take charge of the guitar, and then wait for other classmates to take over my shift."

"What time are you on duty?"

"From eight to nine," Li Luo said. "What about you?"

"I'm about the same." Ying Chanxi nodded happily. "Then after I'm done, I'll come to your class to find you, and we can go collect stamps together, okay?"

Li Luo smiled and nodded in agreement. "Okay."

"What about Zhusheng?" Ying Chanxi asked in a low voice. "Does she want to join us then?"

"Her? She probably won't have much free time in the morning," Li Luo said with a laugh. "The 'Guess the Instrument' game was her idea."

"But in our class, there are only about six or seven people who can play different instruments."

"We can't just have these few people busy in the classroom the whole time and not let them go play in other classrooms."

"It just so happens that Zhusheng really likes this mini-game, so she plans to stay in the classroom the entire morning to be in charge of all the different instruments."

Ying Chanxi was a little stunned after hearing this. "Then, that's really tough on her."

"By the way, what mini-game did your class finally decide on?" Li Luo asked curiously.

"Our class..." Ying Chanxi chuckled twice, covering her forehead in resignation. "It ended up being a Sudoku game."

"It's a 3x3 grid, and we'll fill in six numbers beforehand."

"Then, as long as someone can fill in the remaining three numbers correctly, they pass."

"...Worthy of being Class One." Li Luo didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

"So what are your plans for the afternoon?" Ying Chanxi asked again. "It's the club experience activity in the afternoon, right?"

"The afternoon will probably be very busy, I don't know if I'll have any time." Li Luo thought for a moment and said, "Aren't we scheduled for the same shift at the literature club's booth? After I'm done there, I still have to go help at the rock club. That club has few members, so I don't know if I can spare any time."

"Alright then." Ying Chanxi was slightly disappointed. "I'll go hang out with Xinyan then."

After the dishes were done, Yan Zhusheng stayed for a little while longer before taking her leave.

Before she left, she didn't forget to help them take the kitchen trash downstairs and throw it out on her way.

The three people at home each returned to their own rooms.

Li Luo and Xu Youyu had to go to their rooms to write, while Ying Chanxi needed to study hard, maintaining her habit of evening self-study from school.

When she was studying at her desk, the Pikachu and Doraemon plushies were placed on either side, guarding her like two door gods.

If she ever got stuck on a problem, Ying Chanxi would randomly pick one and give it a punch. After venting a little, inspiration for the problem would come.

Recently, Ying Chanxi had been thinking about whether she should bring the two plushies to school.

But after some thought, she felt that her classmates would find it a bit childish if they saw them.

Besides, after stuffing these two plushies into her schoolbag, there wouldn't be much room left for books.

So, the idea was eventually dropped.

Meanwhile, as Li Luo was writing, the QQ icon in the bottom right corner of his screen suddenly started flashing.

At first, Li Luo thought it was his editor looking for him.

But upon closer inspection, he saw it was a certain investment expert.

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: Big shot, your book just debuted on the City-Life bestseller list and it's already reached second place. That's really quite an amazing feat.

The premium author group for the City-Life category has also been discussing your book all day. There's no shortage of envy, jealousy, and hate.

Most people are just envious.

A few believe Li Luo was purely lucky, that he only got a huge slice of the pie thanks to the traffic from the song "Annual Rings".

They think if the same amount of traffic were directed to their own books, the results definitely wouldn't be any worse than "I'm Really Not a Star".

As a veteran who had surfed the internet for decades in his past life, Li Luo couldn't be bothered to respond to such claims and almost never chatted in that premium author group.

Chong Ran: It's alright. Thanks to others helping direct traffic, otherwise it wouldn't have had such a good result.

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: That's your own skill too. After all, you wrote "Annual Rings".

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: Is it convenient to share your stats? How many average subscriptions do you have now?

Asked this question, Li Luo opened his author dashboard to take a look, then replied.

Chong Ran: Over 8,700.

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: So fast! I'm only at 2,700... I just got a new feature recommendation today, I wonder if I can break 3,000.

Chong Ran: Trust me, your book has the potential for ten thousand subscriptions. Just keep writing well, and you'll get there sooner or later. Getting premium status will be a piece of cake for you.

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: Hahaha, you're too good with your compliments. Even I don't have that much confidence.

Chong Ran: Then we can make a bet. I bet your book will reach ten thousand subscriptions.

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: Uh-huh? You're that confident in my book? What do you want to bet?

Chong Ran: I haven't thought about that. Is there anything you want to bet?

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: Let me think. There doesn't seem to be anything. How about the loser agrees to do one thing for the other person, as long as it's within their power.

Chong Ran: Sure. Then I'll start thinking about what to make you do.

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: Hey hey! Don't be so confident in me! You make it sound like you've already won.

Chong Ran: So you have that little confidence in yourself?

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: It's mainly because I've been having a headache with the plot recently. A female supporting character is kind of stealing the show, and I don't know how to pull it back.

When Li Luo was bored, he would sometimes read the book Xu Youyu was writing.

Even though he had already read it once in his past life, the interesting thing was that ever since Xu Youyu got to know him, the content she wrote had gradually deviated from the "Era of Literature and Art" that existed in his memory.

A lot of the content and plot points already didn't match up.

In other words, the Xu Youyu of this life, under the influence of the butterfly wings he had flapped, could no longer write the same "Era of Literature and Art" from his past life.

But Li Luo's impression from reading it was that the current "Era of Literature and Art" was more down-to-earth and interesting in its character interactions and depictions of daily life.

Especially some of the details of the male and female leads' lives, which had a very slice-of-life feel. Sometimes, he even got a strange sense of déjà vu while reading.

It was hard for Li Luo to say whether this change was for the better or worse, but he knew one thing very clearly: this change had become uncontrollable ever since he met Xu Youyu after his rebirth.

Sometimes, when you caught a flash of inspiration, your fingers would fly across the keyboard, and you could write an incredibly exciting plot.

But if you were suddenly interrupted mid-flow, by the time you touched the keyboard again, you might never be able to re-enter that previous state, and the originally brilliant plot would be lost.

Chong Ran: If you've already set it in stone as a single female lead, then try to consciously cut down her scenes.

Chong Ran: Web novels are serialized literature. When readers follow along for a long time, once a character starts to fade into the background, their feelings for that character will gradually weaken.

Chong Ran: My suggestion is that you think carefully again about the female lead's own shining qualities.

Chong Ran: A lot of the time, in order to show off the female lead's attractive points early on, we end up writing her character too thoroughly all at once.

Chong Ran: As a result, readers quickly get tired of a character who's been fully fleshed out, and they turn their interest to another character who can bring a sense of novelty.

In his past life's "Era of Literature and Art", there was actually a similar problem.

After all, an outstanding male lead who was an actor would definitely interact with various female celebrities.

But SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller had always maintained the single female lead storyline. Those female celebrities who appeared occasionally basically vanished after a plot climax.

Only the female lead always remained by the protagonist's side.

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: Thanks for the guidance, I'll think about it some more!

Chong Ran: Just don't forget what you promised me if you lose the bet.

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: What if you lose? Be careful, I might make you do something embarrassing.

Chong Ran: Like what?

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: Like personally recommending your own book to your family and friends?

Chong Ran: You're kind of vicious.

Chong Ran: But you have given me a pretty good idea.

Chong Ran: If you lose, why don't we go with this punishment?

SleepingEarlyWillMakeYouTaller: No way! I'll die!

(End of this chapter)
